title: Citrine marketplace certification + KMS & billing integration sync
summary: Sync to align on Citrine's marketplace listing requirements, KMS/HSM compatibility, billing/metering expectations, and UAT acceptance criteria. Redwood SE walked through KMS integration patterns (customer-managed keys, transit vs data-at-rest), suggested onprem connector auth flow, and proposed a benchmarking plan for token latency and quantized model variants. Action items: Redwood to share KMS playbook and billing metering spec; Citrine to provide sample payloads and UAT testbed access; schedule UAT pilot week of 6/15.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-27 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 53 min | Location: Zoom | Attendees: 8 (Redwood AE/SE + Citrine platform/security/product)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the marketplace checklist. 
[00:12] Daniel (Citrine): Hi, Daniel here. Marta, Omar, Leena are on as well. Thanks. 
[00:20] Alex: Great. Priya from our SE team will run through the KMS and onprem connector patterns. Priya, over to you. 
[00:29] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool, hi all. So first slide—sorry, I'm sharing the runbook link in chat: https://redwood.app/partners/citrine/uat-playbook (note: internal preview). At a high level there are two recommended integration patterns for KMS: customer-managed keys in our cloud (bring-your-own-key, BYOK), or HSM-backed key references for private deployments. 
[00:55] Omar (Citrine): Quick q: our security team requires HSM root of trust, we've got Thales appliances. Do you have an HSM connector? 
[01:06] Priya: Yes, we support KMIP-style HSMs via a translation layer in the private control plane; for hosted we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM, or a customer-managed external KMS through secure tunnels. The caveat is latency—if the KMS call is inline per inference request it's bad, so we use envelope encryption and cache decrypted data keys locally with strict TTL and rotation. 
[01:35] Marta (Citrine): How do you handle rotation—we need a 24-hour forced re-wrap policy. 
[01:42] Priya: We can do re-wrap at the KV cache boundary. Practically we rotate the data key and the runtime will re-wrap prefixes; there's a short window where tokens are still valid, we can tighten it if you need synchronous rotation. Note though that synchronous rotations add tail latency. 
[01:58] Daniel: That's a concern—our SLAs aim for p99 < 120ms for short prompts. 
[02:06] Priya: Understood. For p99 goals we recommend: 1) envelope keys with local cache TTL 10-60 minutes depending on your risk tolerance, 2) colocated KMS or private deployment in your VPC if you need sub-100ms p99, 3) fallback to a less strict rotation for non-sensitive workloads. 
[02:30] Alex: Also note we can do a dedicated capacity pool for Citrine which guarantees latency characteristics, that might be simplest if you want predictable p99. 
[02:40] Leena (Citrine): Cost implications? Dedicated sounds pricey. 
[02:44] Jordan (Partner Ops): We can model cost vs performance—I'll follow up with a pro forma. 
[02:52] [00:03:00] Priya: Next topic: marketplace listing requirements—packaging, connectors, and metering hooks. For Azure marketplace specifically you need an ARM template or managed image. For our hybrid listing we provide a pre-built Helm chart plus a marketplace adapter that emits metering events to the listing's billing system. 
[03:18] Marta: How do we expose metering tags? We need to show per-tenant usage for chargeback. 
[03:25] Priya: The adapter adds standard labels: tenant_id, model_variant, region, and a usage_class (tokens/generated). Metering events are buffered and posted to the marketplace endpoint. We also support a pull model for larger customers. 
[03:38] Omar: Is the metering schema compatible with our internal billing? We use nested JSON for line items. We've run into mapping issues with other vendors. 
[03:47] Priya: We can export both the standard flattened metering CSV and a nested JSON webhook payload. We'll share the spec doc. 
[03:55] Alex: Note added: share billing/metering spec (link in next steps). 
[04:00] [00:04:30] Leena: On the listing side, Marketplace certification also asks for vulnerability scanning and SBOMs. Do you support SBOM generation for the connector? 
[04:10] Tess (Solutions): Yes, our packaging pipeline generates an SPDX SBOM for images and we can provide scan reports from our CI. For on-prem connectors we provide a reproducible build artifact. 
[04:20] Daniel: Good. Can we host the connector in our registry? 
[04:25] Tess: Absolutely, we can provide the Helm chart and clear instructions to pull images from your ACR/ECR during install. 
[04:32] [00:05:00] Priya: Now the onprem auth flow. Two modes: outbound-only connector that opens a TLS tunnel to Redwood control plane, or inbound peering where you create a private VPC peering and we push images into your network. Outbound-only is easiest for air-gapped constraints because no inbound ports required. 
[05:05] Marta: We prefer outbound-only but need SAML/SSO for admin UI. 
[05:12] Alex: We integrate with SAML SSO and support SCIM provisioning. You'll get RBAC mapping in the next revision of the runbook. 
[05:20] [00:05:45] Omar: What about audit logs? We have strict audit retention and need tamper-evident logs. 
[05:28] Priya: Audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (syslog or secure webhooks). For private deployments we support local write-once store and KMS-signed log manifests for tamper detection. 
[05:42] Daniel: Ok. On to quantization: we've got a benchmark showing 8-bit quantization saves ~3-4x cost but there's a slight drop in answer quality on long prompts. 
[05:55] Priya: Right—quantization profiles are workload-dependent. For chatty, context-heavy workloads we'd recommend 4-bit quant with selective FP16 for attention layers (mixed). We propose an A/B UAT to measure regeneration rate and hallucination delta. 
[06:18] Leena: What's the effort to plug that into our evaluation harness? 
[06:22] Priya: Minimal—send sample prompts and expected outputs, we'll run the same evaluation on hosted and a quantized variant and provide metrics. Ideally provide at least 500 prompts that represent edge cases. 
[06:34] Alex: Action item: Citrine to share 500-prompt sample set and CI access for metrics collection. 
[06:40] [00:07:30] Marta: Network requirements—what ports, bandwidth for the connector? Our networking folks need to preapprove. 
[06:47] Priya: For outbound-only, it's HTTPS over 443 to our control plane; for private VPC peering we need route table updates and allow GRE for some legacy tunnels (rare). Bandwidth depends on tokens/sec; we provided a bandwidth calculator in the runbook. 
[07:03] Jordan: I'll attach that calculator and we'll run numbers. 
[07:08] [00:07:50] Daniel: Security questionnaire: there's an item about data residency for logs and embeddings. We need an option to ensure embeddings never leave the EU. 
[07:18] Priya: We support region-restricted routing: embeddings can be pinned to EU clusters, and we can do local-only embeddings for private deployments. For hosted mode, we can ensure the compute and storage live in the selected region. 
[07:33] Omar: Any drift in model performance across regions? 
[07:37] Priya: Slight variance due to different hardware stacks and quantization kernels. We test each region's profile and publish perf/quality deltas in the model catalog. We'll highlight that in the listing. 
[07:50] [00:08:30] Leena: Can Redwood host a trial tenant in EU for us to validate? 
[07:54] Alex: Yes, we can spin up a EU-dedicated trial under a short-term commit—I'll propose options. 
[07:59] [00:09:00] Priya: Switching to acceptance criteria for UAT: we recommend three buckets—functional correctness (matching prompt/response expectations), latency (p99 within agreed target), and security/compliance (KMS validated, SSO/SCIM, audit exports). Each bucket must have pass/fail tests. 
[09:13] Daniel: For latency we'll start with p95 < 80ms, p99 < 200ms during UAT, subject to dedicated pool. 
[09:22] Priya: Noted. For functional correctness we need tolerance thresholds—Leena, can you confirm what percent of prompts can be allowed to deviate? 
[09:30] Leena: We can't exceed 4% divergence for high-critical prompts, 10% for exploratory. We'll attach categories. 
[09:36] [00:09:50] Alex: Let's talk timelines: Citrine wants marketplace listing by end of Q3. That gives us ~9 weeks for certification and UAT. Is that realistic? 
[09:50] Daniel: We're aiming for Q3 as well, but marketplace procurement review can add a 2-week buffer. 
[09:57] Jordan: If we start pilot week of 6/15 we can likely meet Q3 assuming no major security blockers. 
[10:03] [00:10:30] Marta: Benchmarks—can Redwood run a runbook of our sample workload and give granular per-token latency across model variants? We've had noisy numbers from other vendors. 
[10:12] Priya: Yes—we'll run a harness. Please provide sample payloads and expected concurrency. We'll return a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and cache hit rates. 
[10:25] Leena: We'll share by EOD Friday. 
[10:28] [00:10:55] Omar: One more security question: do you support KMS attestations or HSM-backed key attestation for compliance? 
[10:35] Priya: We can provide cryptographic attestations and KMS audit logs. For HSM attestation we rely on the underlying cloud provider's attestation or your on-prem HSM's attestation protocols; we can ingest signed manifests. 
[10:49] Alex: Important note: for marketplace certification the auditor will want CICD artifacts, SBOM, pentest summary. We'll consolidate and provide a certification pack. 
[11:00] [00:11:20] Daniel: Pricing—how will charges show up? We need per-tenant breakouts for the marketplace and a separate pass-through for dedicated capacity if we take that path. 
[11:10] Jordan: Two options: 1) marketplace meter with our adapter pushing tenant-level metrics (we map to marketplace SKUs), or 2) direct billing under a reserved capacity contract with monthly invoice and tenant-level usage tags. We'll share both templates. 
[11:24] [00:11:50] Priya: During UAT we'll enable verbose telemetry so you can reconcile costs. Expect some delta between estimated and billed during the first month as caches warm up. 
[11:36] [00:12:10] Leena: Is there a sandbox marketplace listing we can preview? 
[12:14] Tess: We can share a staging listing and a short demo video of the install flow. I'll put that link in chat. 
[12:20] [00:12:40] Daniel: Any blockers you foresee? 
[12:45] Priya: Biggest technical risks: KMS latency if you require synchronous key fetches, and model quality regressions with aggressive quantization. Operational risk: marketplace certification timeline if SBOM and pentest reports aren't ready. 
[13:00] Alex: We'll mitigate KMS latency with envelope keys and recommend private deployment for strict SLAs. For quantization we'll run A/B and set guardrails. 
[13:09] [00:13:30] Leena: Okay, let's capture next steps and owners. 
[13:35] Alex: Jordan will send the billing/metering spec and cost model. Priya will share the KMS/HSM integration guide and run the initial benchmark. Tess will share SBOM and staging listing link. Citrine to send sample prompts and a sandbox cluster for UAT week. 
[13:58] Marta: We'll try to provide the sample prompts by Friday and open a UAT VPC the week of 6/15. 
[14:08] Omar: We'll also share our security questionnaire answers; expect some followup. 
[14:15] [00:14:40] Alex: Any final questions? 
[14:22] Daniel: None from me, appreciate the clarity. 
[14:27] Priya: Thanks—we'll follow up with a detailed runbook and timeline. 
[14:31] Alex: End of call, thanks everyone.
